title: Ravensgate returns and refunds engine

act2.summary: a supplier recall arrives - a new return reason with its own refund rule, unaffected by restock disposition or notification channel

solutions.title: One shared function decides the refund, by reason
solutions.tradeoff: This route bet that the refund-by-reason branching was the pressure most likely to grow a new member, and pulled it into one function shared by both entry points. The recall arrives on exactly that axis: one new branch, one place, 5 lines across 2 hunks.

solutions.title: One shared function decides the restock disposition, by condition
solutions.tradeoff: This route bet that restock disposition was the pressure worth relieving first, and pulled it into one function shared by both entry points - a reasonable bet the warehouse floor would have applauded. The recall doesn't touch that axis at all: refund-by-reason branching was never touched, so it still duplicates the new branch across both entry points, at exactly the no-pattern baseline's cost.

reviewFocus: Does the reader's own restructuring name, honestly, which of the three pressures (refund by reason, restock by condition, notification by method) it chose to relieve - and does it admit the other two are still duplicated?
Would a reader who restructured a different axis than their own solution's still recognize why the recall lands cheaply or expensively, from the measured numbers alone?
Does the WALKTHROUGH.md for the losing route say plainly that its bet didn't pay off for this act 2, without pretending its own restructuring was worthless in general?
Do both routes agree, byte for byte, with src/ on every act-1 outcome before the recall exists?
